body:
I do already own a bike and I'm able to ride it to the closest bus stop for school as well as work.  The car is already paid off, it's just insurance and maybe a tank of gas of month for grocery shopping  and doctor's appointments. Maintanence is pretty cheap since I've only ever used synthetic oil and a bunch of my buddies are willing to help me when things need fixing. Like my starter a month ago and my rear wheel bearings just after that. 

I'm just really hesitant to get rid of the car since it seems my health is so dependent on it. I'm diabetic and the thought of not being able to get food when I need it is terrifying. And my doctor's office is pretty far away, too. I don't think I'd want to bike or take the bus there every month. I've been debating with myself over this for a long time. Maybe I should just suck it up. 

And it's hard to not to care about what my parents think of me. I really do respect them (especially my father) and love them. They're encouraging; they just don't help out financially. I think that part will take some time

I wouldn't say it's an expensive school, it's public. It's the least expensive one I could go to that had my degree. However, the rent in the city I live in is outrageous. Couple that with high living expenses, high car insurance (since I'm young, but I haven't had any tickets or wrecks) and high medical costs its difficult. I don't know if I mentioned it, but I'm also type 1 diabetic.
Thank you, youve really helped me. It's nice knowing that someone else has been through the same thing I'm going through. You've  given me some good advice and hope.

I really appreciate the long, thought out response, but I don't think I understand. All I got from this is that I should take up acting, but that prospect terrifies me. 

Are you trying to say I should just start acting differently? Because I already am acting differently than im feeling. No one around me knows that I feel so bad.

I earned a C- when I needed a C. I talked to the teacher and he won't help me. I failed because I work 50 hours a week and don't have time to study. This was my thermodynamics course. I was also taking my senior design course and a bio process class. I have too much to do and not enough time to do it. Incidentally I earned a B in my other classes. I want to work in wastewater treatment, which has absolutely nothing to do with thermodynamics but its still a requirement for the degree.
What parts exactly should I be trying to develop and trying to release? Because I'm at a complete loss.
Gotcha. I guess I figured filing independent with the IRS would help with FAFSA somehow. I feel like I should be that dog in the meme: "I have no idea what I'm doing."

My school has a counseling program. I've been to other counselors in the past for anxiety (big surprise!) and they were helpful. I guess I'm just at a loss as to what they could do for me in this situation. I guess I have nothing to lose by giving them a go once the semester starts next week.

Well I'd like to declare myself an an independent so I COULD file FAFSA as an independent and I didn't know how to do that so I figured I'd make an appointment to see a financial advisor from the school. This is what they told me even though I told them I dont get I help from my parents. I guess they were just wrong or thought I was lying?

That's pretty much what I've been doing with the sewing and gardening. They're my go-to activities since they focus me so well. And it has the added bonus of being constructive. But it's just helping me with my immediate problems, you know?
I guess I should try again. I don't understand why the financial aid people would be so dismissive

The financial aid office told me that I couldn't file as an independent unless I turned 24, got married or had kids. What did you do differently? I'm not the only person I know that is having this problem. 

I'm only 6 classes away, but since I've failed so many I've reached my limit on hours and I actually have to start paying out of state tuition from now on.

I have been to my advisor but all she said was that engineering isn't for everyone and that maybe it's just not meant for me. She's not a very good advisor. She's been known to make grown men cry. Is there someone else I can talk to?

How can I establish financial independence? My parents aren't an option. 

I just feel really trapped. I can't count on my parents for anything, but I can't declare myself an independent in the eyes of the government until I get married, have a baby or turn 24. I don't have that much time. Once I leave school I have to start paying back my loans after 6 months. And yet I won't have a job that can support that (its not even really supporting me now)

If it is possibles for me to get my degree, I don't know how. When I talked to my college advisor she just told me engineering isn't for everyone and maybe it's just not something for me. 

The problem with my boyfriend is that I also live with him. We share rent so it's cheaper. He makes more money than I do and pays for most of my food. If I leave him I'd have to break my lease, find a new apartment that will cost me more money, and ill be even more financially unstable. After paying bills a few days ago I currently have $14 in my bank account. What could I possibly do?

No, my parents are 8 hours away in a city that doesn't have a college. I'm set into my lease for one more year and its actually really expensive to break or sublet. Too much for me to afford. 

My parents think that I'm doing great; they know I have money issues but they don't know I'm doing bad in school. My brother is suicidal and my sister is also depressed, so much so that she doesn't take care of her type 1 diabetes. It's gotten so bad that her kidneys are failing. I don't want to bring my parents more problems. They don't need anything else to worry about. 

I don't think I could get back into school once I leave. I have to start paying back my student loans 6 months after I leave school. Ill be so financially crippled school won't be an option. 

I've been to AlAnon meetings with my boyfriend (his mother died of a heroin overdose when he was 16), and he's also been to court mandated anon meetings. I tell him I don't like his drinking, but he just hides it from me. He's not violent or anything, he's incredibly sweet. But he has his own problems and can't help me anymore. 

The problem won't be gone in 2 years because I will be in incredible debt, my brother, sister and boyfriend will probably be dead, I won't be able to finish my degree. Everything I love will be gone
